name: Receive and accession specimens at the laboratory
summary: Couriers bring totes of specimens from collection centres, clinics and homes to the regional laboratories, mostly in waves in the late afternoon and evening. Processing lab assistants check the totes against manifests and transport temperature, unpack and scan each tube into the LIS, key in orders from clinics' paper requisitions, check each specimen against acceptance criteria and route tubes to the automation line, departments, other company laboratories or outside laboratories. Clinic requisitions with missing information, mislabelled or unlabelled tubes, haemolysed or clotted specimens and missing bags cause holds, calls, rejections and patient recollections.

baseline.org_archetype: A large private community laboratory company with regional laboratories receiving about 40,000 specimens a day, a central LIS and pre-analytical automation feeding chemistry track lines.
baseline.notes: Most work arrives already registered at a collection centre, so receipt is a barcode scan; only clinic-collected requisitions are keyed at the laboratory.

trigger: A courier tote containing the requisition's specimens arrives at the laboratory receiving bench.
end_state: All acceptable specimens are received in the LIS and placed on the testing line or department racks, packed for another site or sent out; unacceptable ones are rejected and logged.

volume.seasonality: Daily surge from late afternoon to midnight as routes return; lower on weekends; follows collection centre volumes.

evidence.note: Org file process map and demand driver d_community_reqs (estimate consistent with 40,000 specimens a day at about 1.7 specimens per requisition).

Org file role and cost. Posting pays $19.75 to $23.50 an hour in 2026, consistent with the org file's Job Bank based cost. FTE estimate: most of the 150 processing assistants' time, the rest on result reporting and interlab transfers; shifts cover the evening and overnight surge.
Org file role and cost; reviews label and specimen problems, signs off rejections and exceptions, and runs shift huddles; estimate.

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Courier routing, dispatch and web-based order and tracking system
Quality management system software (document control, CAPA, training records)
Pre-analytical automation and track input modules (centrifuge, decapper, aliquotter, sorter)

steps.name: Receive courier totes and check them against the manifest
steps.description: A processing lab assistant signs for the totes at the receiving bench, scans each tote or bag barcode into the tracking system and checks the count against the courier's manifest for that route or centre.

error.defect_description: Tote received but not scanned, so it shows as missing.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus pre-examination requirements: chain of receipt and traceability of specimens from collection site to laboratory

next.condition: bag or tote missing from the manifest

evidence.note: Common receiving practice; per-requisition share of tote handling and the evening queue are estimates (routes return in waves late afternoon and evening).

steps.name: Check transport temperature and condition
steps.description: The lab assistant checks that refrigerated and frozen boxes arrived cold or frozen, reads the temperature indicator where one is used, and looks for leaking or broken containers before opening bags.

error.defect_description: Temperature excursion not noticed.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus: transport conditions monitored and specimen integrity checked on receipt; TDG Category B containment

evidence.note: Specimen acceptability protocols (dyn_licences) and packaging rules (tdg_regs); share is an estimate.

steps.name: Unpack bags and sort by temperature, priority and type
steps.description: The lab assistant opens the biohazard bags, separates requisitions from tubes, pulls out STAT and short-stability specimens first, and groups tubes by temperature and department so frozen and urgent work is handled before routine tubes.

error.defect_description: Tube separated from its bag or requisition.

next.condition: order already registered at a collection centre or by mobile staff
paper requisition from a clinic, needs order entry

evidence.note: Pre-registered share from the org file: 560,000 centre visits and about 26,000 mobile collections of 690,000 requisitions; times are estimates.

steps.name: Scan tubes to receive them in the LIS
steps.description: The lab assistant scans each tube's barcode; the LIS records the receipt time, shows the ordered tests and expected tubes, and the assistant checks the tube count and types against the order on screen.

error.defect_description: Tube received under the wrong order or tube type not checked.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus: date and time of specimen receipt recorded and specimens checked against the request

next.condition: tube missing, extra or wrong type
label unreadable, missing or does not match

evidence.note: Barcode receipt is standard LIS practice; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a missing or mismatched tube
steps.description: The lab assistant searches the other bags from the same centre, checks the collection comment in the LIS, and calls the centre if needed. A test whose tube never arrived is cancelled with a comment asking for recollection, and the rest of the order goes on.
outputs: tube found or test cancelled with comment

error.defect_description: Tube matched to the wrong order.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimates.

steps.name: Check a paper requisition against its specimens
steps.description: For clinic-collected work the lab assistant checks the requisition for clinician, signature, health number and tests, and compares the patient's name and date of birth on each tube label with the requisition, plus the collection date and time.

error.defect_description: Missing requisition field or label mismatch not noticed.

control.basis: Laboratory and Specimen Collection Centre Licensing Act requisition requirements and the laboratory's specimen acceptance criteria

next.condition: unlabelled tube or label does not match requisition

evidence.note: Posting describes checking identification and data entry; shares are estimates. Clinic-collected work has more problems than centre-registered orders.

steps.name: Enter the order in the LIS and label the tubes
steps.description: The lab assistant finds or creates the patient, keys health number, clinician and tests from the requisition, prints LIS barcode labels and applies them next to the clinic's labels, and scans the requisition into the imaging system.

error.defect_description: Test missed or wrong test, clinician or patient keyed.

evidence.note: 4.8% of outpatient requisitions had an order entry error in the Q-Probes study; entry time is an estimate.

steps.name: Inspect specimens for acceptability
steps.description: While handling the tubes the lab assistant looks for clotted EDTA tubes, visible haemolysis, underfilled citrate tubes, leaking containers, wrong tube types and specimens past their stability time, against the laboratory's acceptance criteria.

error.defect_description: Unacceptable specimen passed to the bench.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus: documented specimen acceptance and rejection criteria applied on receipt

next.condition: acceptable; already spun or no spin needed

evidence.note: Specimen rejection 0.2% of specimens (epmc_rejection) to 4.4% in some hospital labs (ag17); haemolysis flagged in 3.5% of outpatient specimens but mostly reported with comments (tian22). Per-requisition problem share of 1.2% is set within this range.

steps.name: Hold the requisition and call the clinic
steps.description: The lab assistant puts the specimens in the hold rack or fridge, logs the problem, and phones or faxes the clinic for the missing health number, clinician or test, usually on the day shift after the evening receiving rush.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimates.

steps.name: Verify the entered order against the requisition image
steps.description: A second lab assistant or the same one at a later pass compares the entered order with the scanned requisition, checking patient, clinician and every test, and corrects any discrepancy before results are released.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Laboratory order entry verification procedure (recheck of manually entered orders against the requisition)

evidence.note: Rechecking entered orders against requisitions was associated with lower error rates; the share caught is an estimate.

steps.name: Supervisor reviews a labelling or specimen problem
steps.description: The processing supervisor examines the specimen and paperwork, decides whether it must be rejected, can be accepted with a comment, or, for an irreplaceable specimen such as tissue or fluid, needs the collector to come in and identify it with documented sign-off.

error.defect_description: Specimen accepted that should have been rejected.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus specimen acceptance criteria: mislabelled or unlabelled specimens are not relabelled except documented exceptions for irreplaceable specimens

next.condition: accept with comment or after documented identification

evidence.note: Specimen acceptability protocols (dyn_licences); mislabelling rates (epmc_mislabel). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Reject the specimen and log a nonconformance
steps.description: The lab assistant cancels the affected tests in the LIS with the rejection code, so the report tells the clinician the specimen was unsuitable and must be recollected, and records the event in the nonconformance log with the collection site.

error.defect_description: Wrong test cancelled.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus: rejected specimens documented, requester informed and nonconformances recorded for trend review

evidence.note: Rejection documentation is part of the QMS; times are estimates.

steps.name: Clinic supplies the missing information
steps.description: The clinic calls back, faxes a corrected requisition or uploads it. If nothing arrives before the specimen's stability runs out, the tests are cancelled and a recollection is requested.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: no reply within stability; cancel and request recollection

evidence.note: Common practice; clinic response times are estimates.

steps.name: Centrifuge specimens that arrived unspun
steps.description: Tubes from clinics and other sites that were not spun before transport are loaded into the laboratory centrifuge or the automation line's centrifuge module after clotting, spun and checked.

error.defect_description: Tube spun incorrectly or broken in the centrifuge.

evidence.note: Most centre specimens are spun before pickup; share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Aliquot specimens for several departments or sites
steps.description: When one tube must feed tests in different departments or another laboratory, the lab assistant or the automation line pours off labelled aliquots; manual aliquots are needed for tests off the track or going to another site.

error.defect_description: Aliquot mislabelled.

evidence.note: Per-requisition share of manual aliquoting is an estimate; most chemistry aliquots are made on the line.

steps.name: Load tubes onto the automation line or department racks
steps.description: The lab assistant places chemistry and immunoassay tubes on the automation input, haematology tubes in analyser racks, and microbiology, cytology and pathology specimens in the department bins, checking the LIS routing for each.

error.defect_description: Specimen put in the wrong department rack and delayed.

next.condition: test done at another company laboratory
test done by an outside laboratory

evidence.note: Routing shares are estimates from the org file's interlab transfer (about 4,000 a month) and send-out (about 6,000 a month) volumes; interlab is raised to cover routine specialty work moved in batches.

steps.name: Pack specimens for another company laboratory
steps.description: The lab assistant puts specimens for tests done at another company laboratory in a labelled transfer rack, lists them on the interlab manifest in the LIS and packs them in a Category B transport box at the right temperature for the next line haul.

error.defect_description: Specimen left off the manifest or packed at the wrong temperature.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations section 1.39: UN3373 Category B packaging, mark and 24-hour number

evidence.note: Packaging rule from tdg_regs; times are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare a send-out to an outside laboratory
steps.description: For a test no company laboratory performs, the lab assistant creates the send-out request in the LIS, prints the outside laboratory's requisition or manifest, and places the specimen in the send-out rack for the reference team.

error.defect_description: Wrong test or specimen type requested from the outside lab.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimates.

steps.name: Trace a missing bag with the courier and the centre
steps.description: The lab assistant checks the tracking scans for the stop, calls the dispatcher and the collection centre, and asks the courier to check the vehicle. A specimen that cannot be found is logged as lost and the patient is called back for recollection.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus: investigation and recording of lost specimens as nonconformances

evidence.note: Common practice; estimates.

steps.name: Notify the client that a recollection is needed
steps.description: The lab assistant faxes or phones the rejection notice to the clinic for clinic-collected work, or adds the patient to the collection centre's recollection call list, so someone contacts the patient to come back.

error.defect_description: Notice not sent, so the patient is never recalled.

next.condition: other specimens on the order are acceptable

evidence.note: Common practice; who calls the patient varies by site; estimates.

exceptions.name: Clinic requisition with missing information
exceptions.description: Specimens are held while the clinic is asked for the health number, clinician or test; if no reply comes within the specimen's stability, the tests are cancelled.

exceptions.name: Missing or mismatched tube
exceptions.description: The tube count or type does not match the order; the assistant searches bags and calls the centre, and cancels a test whose tube never arrived.

exceptions.name: Mislabelled, unlabelled or unacceptable specimen
exceptions.description: The supervisor reviews and usually rejects the specimen; tests are cancelled with a recollection comment and a nonconformance is logged.

exceptions.name: Temperature excursion or leak in transport
exceptions.description: A box arrives warm or thawed or a container has leaked; affected specimens go to the supervisor for a decision.

exceptions.name: Missing bag on the manifest
exceptions.description: A bag on the courier manifest is not in the tote; the assistant traces it through tracking scans, the dispatcher and the centre.

exceptions.name: Order entry error found on verification
exceptions.description: The check of a manually entered order against the requisition image finds a discrepancy, which is corrected.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from tote arrival at receiving to specimens at the testing line or bench (0.05 days is 72 minutes)
benchmarks.population: High-volume community laboratory receiving, evening surge included

evidence.note: No published benchmark found; estimate from the evening receiving surge and short handling times. Problem requisitions waiting for clinics take up to two days.

benchmarks.population: Hospital laboratories in Ontario (0% to 4.4%, 2016/17) and 21 million venous specimens in 10 hospitals (0.197%)

evidence.note: Definitions differ between studies.

benchmarks.population: 660 laboratories in the CAP Q-Probes program

pain_points.description: Most totes arrive in the late afternoon and evening, so receiving queues build and short-stability specimens compete with routine work.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

pain_points.description: Clinic requisitions are keyed by hand at the laboratory, with order entry errors and holds when information is missing.

evidence.note: 4.8% of outpatient requisitions with an order entry error.

pain_points.description: Mislabelled, haemolysed, clotted and underfilled specimens found at receipt force patient recollection days after the visit.

evidence.note: Rejection and haemolysis rates.

pain_points.description: Bags missing from manifests take hours of calls between the laboratory, dispatch and centres to trace.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Specimen rejection rate (share of times a test cannot be done due to a mistake in collecting or handling specimens) ranged from 0% to 4.4% in a sample of Ontario hospital laboratories in 2016/17; laboratories must take part in the IQMH quality management program to be licensed.

sources.title: Europe PMC abstracts: pre-analytical error and specimen rejection studies (Xie et al. 2026, 21 million venous specimens; Alenezy et al. 2025)
sources.supports: Xie et al.: pooled venous specimen rejection rate 0.197% of 21,319,200 specimens in 10 hospitals; leading causes clotting, insufficient or incorrect volume and container errors; outpatient events more often order, timing or identification errors. Alenezy et al.: 0.063% of 3,346,199 test orders repeated or rejected for pre-analytical errors, mostly clotted (32%) and insufficient (31%).

sources.title: Outpatient order accuracy: a College of American Pathologists Q-Probes study of requisition order entry accuracy in 660 institutions (abstract)
sources.publisher: Archives of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, via Europe PMC
sources.supports: 4.8% of 114,934 outpatient requisitions had at least one order entry error; rechecking entered orders against the requisition and monitoring accuracy were associated with lower error rates.

sources.title: Europe PMC abstracts: specimen labelling and identification error studies (Raymond et al. 2024; Ning et al. 2016; Sandhu et al. 2017)
sources.supports: Identified mislabelling 1.15 per 1,000 specimens with occult mislabelling estimated at 3.17 per 1,000 (Raymond); outpatient identification errors 0.0067% of specimens before barcode interventions (Ning).

sources.title: The incidence rate and influence factors of hemolysis, lipemia, icterus in fasting serum biochemistry specimens
sources.supports: Haemolysis index flagged 3.54% of outpatient serum specimens; specimens with longer transfer time had more haemolysis, lipaemia and icterus.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: Brampton, London, Ottawa and Peterborough laboratories are accredited to ISO 15189 by Accreditation Canada and licensed by the Ontario ministry; Winnipeg holds MANQAP accreditation; the QMS includes specimen acceptability protocols, computerized systems validation, corrective and preventive action and monitoring of key indicators.

sources.title: Lab Assistant Specimen Processing, Brampton (job posting #2026-12366)
sources.supports: Processing specimens and entering requisitions accurately and on time; ensuring samples are properly identified, data entered and labelled; following protocols for unsuitable samples; high-volume, time-sensitive environment; 10 am to 6 pm shift with rotating weekends; $19.75 to $23.50 an hour; AS400 data entry system/LIS knowledge an asset.

sources.title: Wages: Medical Laboratory Technical Assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $17.95, median $26.25, high $36.00 (2023-2024).

sources.title: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (SOR/2001-286), full text
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: UN3373 Biological Substance, Category B must travel in CGSB-43.125 Type P650 containment with the Category B mark, shipping name and a 24-hour number (section 1.39); training certificates required (Part 6).

assumptions: About 88% of requisitions arrive already registered in the LIS by collection centres or mobile staff, so their receipt is a barcode scan; 12% come from clinics with paper requisitions and are keyed at the laboratory. The split is derived from the org file's volumes.
Per-requisition shares of tote handling, unpacking and rack loading are small fractions of a minute because work is done in batches of many requisitions.
Chemistry and immunoassay tubes go through pre-analytical automation; this is inferred from the org file's track-line analysers and is not sourced.

Mean hands-on time is about 2.3 minutes per requisition, which at 690,000 requisitions a month implies about 200 FTE at 130 productive hours, against 131 FTE stated; the org file has 150 processing assistants who also report results and pack interlab transfers.
The process ends when specimens reach the testing line or department racks; testing waits belong to the testing workflows.
Rejection here covers specimens rejected at receipt. Haemolysis found later by analyser indices is handled in testing.
Loaded costs come from the org file (hourly wage times 1.35).
